newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Sale of Ivory Coast state sugar firm due Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Sale of Ivory Coast state sugar firm due Wednesday.

text.p: The successful bidders for Ivory Coast's state sugar company SODESUCRE will be announced on Wednesday June 4, an official at the country's Privatisation Committee said on Tuesday.
An advertisement in the official Fraternite-Matin daily said bids had to be with the committee by 1800 GMT on Tuesday.

The government announced the plan to sell SODESUCRE in June 1996, when it said the company would be split into two, with each unit comprising two processing plants and the plantations surrounding them.

It said a 55 percent stake in each of the two new companies would be sold to private investors. Another five percent of the shares would be taken by employees while the state would keep 20 percent and the remaining 20 percent would be floated on the Abidjan bourse.
Fraternite-Matin said in a report that among the interested investors were Britain's ED&F Man, South Africa's Illovo Sugar, Senegal-based group Mimram and an Ivorian company SIFCA.
The companies can bid for both new units, but a single firm will not be allowed to buy both.
